A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MASS study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E are readable and can be matched despite reordering and added experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, optimization-stage ablations, topology analyses, and token-efficiency results, including additional Claude experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds Mistral-Nemo evaluations, GPTSwarm comparisons, prompt-optimizer ablations, and resource-cost results.

M1.justification: The three-stage framework and building blocks remain. Section 3 corrects the written pruning rule: v1 activates a dimension when u > p, whereas v2 rejects it under that condition and explicitly retains u < p in Algorithm 1. This changes the documented selection procedure; the PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same reasoning, multi-hop question-answering, code-generation, and test-output-prediction tasks. V2's Mistral experiments use retained datasets, including the standard HotpotQA setting already evaluated with Claude in v1. Adding another model does not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 8 newly evaluates GPTSwarm against MASS on MATH and HumanEval with Gemini Pro and Flash; v1 only discusses GPTSwarm as related work. The existing main-table comparator sets are retained, making this a focused baseline addition.

E3.justification: V2 adds Mistral-Nemo-12B evaluations using the Claude-table setup, GPTSwarm comparisons with both Gemini backbones, and a Gemini Flash comparison of prompt optimizers. It also adds token and monetary cost measurements. The original dataset splits, task metrics, and default optimization settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially extends the analyses supporting modularity and efficiency. Table 9 tests APE, DSPy, and MIPRO within MASS, while Table 7 adds training and inference resource comparisons beyond v1's optimization trajectories and inference Pareto plot. The original stage and pruning ablations remain.

E5.justification: The existing three-run evaluations, standard deviations, and Figure 2 uncertainty bars are retained. However, the newly added Mistral, GPTSwarm, and optimizer-comparison tables report point estimates without dispersion, extending the results with less complete uncertainty reporting. No increase in run counts or new statistical procedure is documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial numerical evidence in Tables 5 and 7-9: Mistral-Nemo results, training/inference costs, GPTSwarm comparisons, and optimizer variants. For example, Mistral MASS averages 55.9 versus 46.9 for the strongest listed baseline. Table 1, Claude Table 4, and the stage-ablation table are numerically unchanged; the additions are new comparisons, not gains over the earlier same-setting results.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly derives stage-wise API-call cost expressions and explains their scaling with building blocks and agent counts. Section 3 also formalizes the pruned configuration space and budget constraint. The original optimization objective remains, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain: prompts and topology jointly matter, MASS interleaves three optimization stages, and its discovered systems outperform alternatives. V2 emphasizes optimizer and search-space independence in the conclusion, but this was already claimed through v1's plug-and-play description and Appendix A.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion connects debate to factual multi-hop tasks, parallel exploration to reasoning, and execution with reflection to coding. V2 also contrasts graph sparsification with performance improvement and explains selecting cheaper workflows from the Pareto frontier. These extend the interpretation while retaining the original design principles and principal limitations.

D1.justification: Revised Table 3, Algorithm 1, and Appendix B.3 clarify search parameters, pruning and budget checks, and how the retained construction order produces parallel agent chains. Table 7 adds resource accounting. The prompt templates, discovered prompts, split sizes, and main hyperparameter disclosures remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for concurrent MaAS and additional prompt-optimization research, including APE, OPRO, Trace, semantic backpropagation, and TextGrad, while removing the many-shot reasoner and AutoPEFT references. The broader positioning around joint prompt/topology optimization remains.

P1.justification: Experiments now precede Related Work, the topology-influence discussion moves into the method section, and Appendix C gains named subsections. Definitions and pruning explanations are expanded, with localized copyediting and an updated publication footer. Most existing prose and the prompt appendices are retained.

P2.justification: V2 substantially extends the tabular presentation with separate displays for Mistral results, resource costs, GPTSwarm comparisons, and optimizer ablations. Algorithm 1 becomes full-width and Table 3 is restructured with explicit parameter definitions. Existing figures are retained, with Figures 3/4 reordered and appendix displays relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful additional checks of model generality, baseline competitiveness, and optimizer modularity, alongside resource accounting. Correcting the pruning rule and clarifying workflow construction also improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by missing dispersion in the new performance tables and insufficiently specified task/backbone settings in the cost table; the established main results remain unchanged.
